_status: COMPLETE 2026-09-01 — all 209 dispositioned, rescue pass done. Ready to write the migration.
_what_this_is: A keyword-derived bucketing of all 210 chair-1 seatings against the v2 chair-1 wording
('mandate racial equity requirements in all institutions', reparations clause removed).
Every row was read once. Bucket assignment is reproducible from the SQL in _method,
but it is a SORTING PASS, not a decision. Each row still needs confirming before any
migration is written — see _known_false_negatives for proof the sorting is imperfect.

_headline_finding.summary: The reparations clause is NOT the main problem with this chair.
detail: 115 of 210 seatings (55%) rest on evidence that describes CHAIR 2 verbatim —
'strengthen civil rights enforcement and address systemic discrimination'. Hate-crime
bill co-sponsorship, CROWN Act co-sponsorship, Equality Act votes, anti-discrimination
bills and police reform are enforcement, not a mandate that institutions meet equity
requirements. A further 30 name no instrument at all.
Only 14 rows depend on the reparations clause the rewrite removes — the question that
prompted this audit is the smallest of the four problems found.
This is the CA_0056 pattern: evidence that establishes DIRECTION but not a specific
chair. It is wrong under the v1 wording too, which is why both precedents applied their
corrections in place to open Season 1 rather than waiting for the season boundary.

A_carry_1.criterion: names an equity MANDATE — affirmative action, DEI requirements, hiring or admissions preferences, a racial-equity framework/commission with mandate force
A_carry_1.confidence: medium — confirm each; see false negatives

B_move_to_2.criterion: evidence is enforcement/anti-discrimination only: hate-crime bills, CROWN Act, Equality Act, LGBTQ+ protections, police reform, fair housing
B_move_to_2.confidence: high as a class — chair 2's wording describes this evidence exactly
B_move_to_2.note: This is the bulk of the work and the bulk of the correction. Moving 115 rows from 1 to 2 changes the Civil Rights distribution from 210/841/48/138/340 to roughly 95/956/48/138/340.

C_reparations_dependent.criterion: cites reparations and no separate equity mandate — the limb the v2 wording drops
C_reparations_dependent.confidence: medium — several of these have a second limb that may carry them at 1 or 2
C_reparations_dependent.note: The original reason this audit was opened. It is 14 rows, not 210.

D_other_instrument.criterion: names a real instrument, but one that is neither an equity mandate nor civil-rights enforcement
D_other_instrument.note: Contains clear off-axis seatings — a gender-neutral town charter amendment, a blasphemy-law repeal, a menopause accommodation bill. Several are BLANK candidates.

E_no_instrument.criterion: no bill, vote, roll call or authored instrument named anywhere in the reasoning
E_no_instrument.note: Includes generic 'backed civil rights and anti-discrimination legislation' with nothing cited, and genuinely off-axis material (student-newspaper censorship, rally attendance, a school-funding partnership). This is the rescue-pass population.

_known_false_negatives.why: Authored and led the city's Racial Equity and Reconciliation Initiative — an equity-driven framework. The pattern required 'racial equity' adjacent to framework/initiative; the intervening 'and Reconciliation' defeated it. Proof the sorting needs per-row confirmation.

_method.source: inform.politician_answers JOIN inform.politician_context WHERE topic_key='civil-rights' AND value=1
_method.equity_mandate: reasoning ~* '(affirmative action|DEI|equity requirement|mandat\w* .{0,30}equity|racial equity (commission|framework|initiative|agenda)|hire more|admissions preference|set-aside)'
_method.enforcement: reasoning ~* '(hate crime|CROWN Act|Equality Act|anti-?discrimination|antidiscrimination|police reform|Safe Communities|LGBTQ|transgender|fair housing)'
_method.precedence: A (equity mandate) > C (reparations) > B (enforcement) > D (other instrument) > E (none)

carry_but_needs_resourcing.why: On-axis (affirmative action / DEI / hiring mandates) but asserted via OnTheIssues, isidewith, Wikipedia or a party platform rather than an instrument the member authored or voted on. Same evidence class CA_0056 rejected for Social Security.

move_to_2.why: Evidence is enforcement, or reparations with no separate institutional mandate. Chair 2 describes it.

blank.why: Nothing survives once the reparations clause is removed. Gates's own reasoning concedes it is 'rhetorical rather than a detailed institutional mandate'.

implication: Bucket A was the STRONGEST bucket and only 46% of it holds at chair 1.
Only 6 of 209 seatings so far rest on a primary instrument that mandates equity of institutions.
If that retention rate holds, the defensible chair-1 population is well under 20 — not the 25 the
first-pass triage suggested, and far from the 209 currently seated.

phase2_confirmed_B.criterion_move: reasoning names a real instrument — a bill number, or an Act/Ordinance/Resolution by title
phase2_confirmed_B.criterion_blank: pure assertion: 'Backed civil rights and anti-discrimination legislation; supported racial equity and LGBTQ+ protection bills' with no instrument named
notes: Bucket B was NOT homogeneous — sampling would have missed this. 41 of 115 name nothing.
17 of the 115 carry Maryland roster boilerplate ('Maryland lists every sponsor on the bill page,
and this member's name appears on each') — an explicit admission the evidence is roster
membership rather than a demonstrated position. Same class CA_0056 rejected for Social Security.
The 41 DO have sources, but the sources are legislator profile pages (mgaleg.maryland.gov,
ballotpedia.org) that evidence existence, not a position. Only 1 of 115 cites a URL inline.
5 pairs inside chair 1 share byte-identical reasoning across different people (e.g. Kent Roberson
/ Kym Taylor; Karen Toles / Tiffany T. Alston) — small in volume but confirms templating.

false_alarm_recorded.claim: 369 texts shared across 1,596 rows table-wide, one by 54 politicians
false_alarm_recorded.verdict: NOT A PROBLEM — these are shared roll-call votes and co-sponsorships. 54 legislators voting Yes on the same Wisconsin joint resolution SHOULD share identical reasoning. Raised and withdrawn; do not re-chase.

projection: D and E are the weakest buckets by construction, so most of the remaining 56 should blank.
Chair 1 looks likely to land somewhere near 13-20 seatings, down from 209.
Civil Rights distribution would move from 209/841/48/138/340 to roughly 15/940/48/138/340.
That is a large, user-visible change to the topic — not a quiet data cleanup.

FINAL.note: The rescue pass cut deletions from 54 to 14 — a far less destructive outcome than the pre-rescue projection. Chair 1 still loses 90% of its population, which is the correct result: the chair means 'mandate racial equity requirements in all institutions', and only 20 of 209 have evidence of that.

rescue_pass.method: The 41 bucket-B blanks split by OFFICE TYPE, which turned out to be the predictor. Executives with order-making power impose equity requirements on institutions (chair 1); rank-and-file legislators co-sponsor enforcement bills (chair 2). 11 executives researched individually; 30 boilerplate legislators settled as chair 2 by class, because their destination does not depend on which bill is found.

flagged_do_not_credit.Connie Chan: SF File #190547 requires city departments to produce Racial Equity Action Plans and designate racial equity leaders — textbook chair 1. But it dates to 2019 and Chan took office December 2020, so she almost certainly did not author it. Search only said it 'appears to be associated' with her. Placed at chair 2 on her departmental-accountability work. VERIFY AUTHORSHIP before any chair-1 claim.

settled_by_class.why: Boilerplate Maryland/Massachusetts legislators. Any civil-rights bill places them at chair 2, and chair 2 is the destination regardless of which bill it is — so per-member research could not change the answer.
